lines.text: Good afternoon, Mrs Adeyemi, how has the neck been from last time?
Well, from last time the headaches have come back three times a week, I'd guess, though I haven't kept a diary like you asked, and they always start at the back of my head on the left.
Do you get any numbness or tingling in your hands?
Let me have a look at your neck movements. Turning to the left is about half what it should be.
The muscles at the top of your shoulders are pretty tight, especially on the left.
My hunch is that the joints in the upper neck are setting off the headaches, but it may be partly posture as well.
I'll do some massage to those muscles now.
Easier, I'm moving a bit better already.
Tuck your chin in gently as if you're making a double chin, ten times every hour you're at the desk.
Thank you, Mrs Adeyemi, that concludes today's session; we'll see you again in a fortnight.
Mr Fitzgerald? Good afternoon, do come through and take a seat.
Thank you. I've had a pain in my right hip for about a month, it's worse when I walk any distance.
